Exhaustively enumerates labelled graphs with exact probability weights at n=3,4,6 in selected cases, including the counterexample and H=K3 versus non-induced F=P3 at n=4, p=1/3 (160/2187).
correctness.rationale: Conditioning on a fixed h-set being an H-component leaves the complement distributed as G(n−h,p) and rules out straddling copies because F is connected. Summing the conditional-mean differences over component indicators proves the general covariance identity, and the positive expectation factor and unimodality of p^e(1−p)^q give the general induced sign cases. But the P3 specialization in the Finding and Proof drops the complement term. Both conventions need B_n=3[binom(n,3)−binom(n−3,3)]=(9n²−45n+60)/2, not 3 binom(n,3). At n=6, p=1/2, direct exact enumeration yields induced covariance −735/8192, whereas the printed special formula gives −195/2048. The printed non-induced factor likewise has the wrong coefficient for n≥6. The induced root count (two iff n≥4) survives since B_3=3, B_4=12, B_n increases, and max p²(1−p)=4/27. The printed root scales do not survive: the correct scales are p_-∼(sqrt(2)/3)n^−1 and 1−p_+∼(2/9)n^−2, by B_np²(1−p)=1 and B_n∼(9/2)n². The n=4 example is unaffected.
residual_risks: This is a decisive finite counterexample to the special formula, not a refutation of the general identity. The all-n correction follows by algebra from the general identity; it is not a separate validated repaired claim.
